transcript.text: Good evening, everyone. We're here for the preflight meeting on the showcase package. Before I can approve anything, I need to hear the final reports from our technical director and our music rights coordinator. Let's start with the technical director — please give us your final report on the production setup, including the eight-piece live band, the 90-minute performance runtime, and any technical considerations for the audience recording permissions. Then we'll move to the music rights coordinator for the rights and compliance report.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical technical issue. I received the completed power survey from the Harborlight electrician this morning — the theater can safely support a live band only if it is configured as six musicians, not eight, and the electrical load plan permits a maximum performance length of 75 minutes, not 90. I haven't entered this in the production draft yet because the signed survey arrived after the draft was circulated.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical rights issue. I confirmed with the publisher that 'Neon Atlas' is NOT cleared for this live showcase. The publisher approved 'Glass River' as the replacement closing song, but the license prohibits audience recording of the performance. I'm still waiting for the countersigned license scan before I can attach it to the show file.
transcript.speaker: A3

commitments.detail: Update the production draft to reflect six-piece band configuration, 75-minute runtime, and audience recording prohibition per the power survey and license constraints.
Obtain and attach the countersigned license scan for 'Glass River' to the show file, confirming the audience recording prohibition is documented.
Enter the signed power survey results into the production draft to formalize the six-musician and 75-minute limits.
